subject: Output liability carveouts — Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Sally Nguyen <sally.nguyen@novaworks.com>, Novaworks Procurement <procurement@novaworks.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Output liability carveouts — Order Form redlines

Hi Sally / Novaworks team,

Thanks for the productive call yesterday. Attaching our redlines to the Order Form and a short note on the indemnity section where I think we need narrower language to keep things operational. High-level callouts:

- Customer asked to broaden indemnity to cover "any third-party claim arising from outputs". That is very broad and would cover a lot of downstream non-IP complaints.
- Redwood position: we can accept indemnity for third-party IP infringement claims tied to model-generated outputs, with clear carveouts (open-source, pre-existing customer content, training-data-only allegations). We also need a reasonable cap and procedural protections (notice, evidentiary standard, cooperation).
- Defense control: Redwood prefers defense control to avoid inconsistent settlements; customer understandably wants input on settlement terms that affect their business.

Attachments: NW_OrderForm_Redline_20270310.pdf (redline), evidence-request-template.docx (evidence collection checklist).

Can you confirm whether Novaworks is open to the following compromise by EOD Friday (Mar 12)?
1) Indemnity limited to third-party IP infringement claims that specifically assert direct copying or unauthorized use of third-party proprietary content in outputs (not general "harmful" or defamatory outputs);
2) Carveouts for open-source-licensed material and claims that relate solely to model training data (where customer has no specific provenance to show infringement);
3) Cap = 12 months of committed fees under the Order Form (with a $1M floor);
4) Redwood to have initial defense control, but customer must consent to any settlement that would admit liability or impose non-monetary injunctive relief—if customer withholds consent, parties will escalate to the disputing leads.

If that sounds workable we can push an updated redline. If Novaworks needs broader coverage (e.g., full output liability without narrow IP framing) let us know and we can flag for commercial escalation (Markus for concessions).

Best,
Priyom

--

From: Sally Nguyen <sally.nguyen@novaworks.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Novaworks Procurement <procurement@novaworks.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 21:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Output liability carveouts — Order Form redlines

Thanks Priyom — appreciate the summary and attachments. I read the redlines with our legal and procurement. A few points from our side:

- We need an indemnity that covers third-party claims arising from outputs. Our use case is customer-facing chat and search; we cant absorb the risk for copyright or right-of-publicity claims that trigger customer liability to its users.
- We accept some carveouts (open-source broadly is fine), but we cannot accept a training-data-only exclusion that effectively immunizes claims tied to model derivation. We need a clear evidentiary path.
- Regarding caps: 12 months' fees is on the table only if it is multiplied by 3x for reputational risk — otherwise we want a higher floor.
- Defense control: customer insists on having decision rights over settlement when the remedy could materially affect our operations (e.g., injunctions, removal of core content). We would be okay with Redwood leading defense but want approval rights on settlements.

Attaching a short note with our proposed language (NW_proposed_indemnity.txt). Can Kimberly or Ben confirm Redwoods legal/customer ops posture? Also: we need SOC2 Type 2 attestation included as an order form attachment and a KMS/HSM note for encryption of customer data — procurement will conditionally approve on these items.

Sally
Sally Nguyen
Head of Legal Operations
Novaworks
sally.nguyen@novaworks.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sally Nguyen <sally.nguyen@novaworks.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 08:22:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Output liability carveouts — Order Form redlines

Sally / Priyom / Ben,

Thanks for the note, Sally. Quick legal read and suggested path:

1) Scope narrowing: We can accept indemnity for third-party IP infringement claims that specifically allege unauthorized copying/use of third-party proprietary content in a Redwood response (i.e., model-generated output), subject to the following:
   - The claim must identify the allegedly infringed material with reasonable particularity (citation/manifestation).
   - Claims that relate solely to the model training process (i.e., "model training inference" allegations without identification of reproductions in outputs) will be excluded unless the customer can point to discrete outputs that reproduce third-party content.

2) Carveouts: Open-source materials (properly licensed) and customer-supplied content are excluded from Redwoods indemnity obligations.

3) Defense/settlement: Redwood requests initial defense control to manage discovery and technical defenses, with a requirement to consult the customer on settlement terms that would entail a non-monetary remedy or admission of liability. If the customer reasonably withholds consent, parties will escalate to senior commercial/legal leads; we can include a mediation step before unilateral action.

4) Cap: Proposed compromise = the greater of $1,000,000 or 12 months of committed fees under the Order Form. If Novaworks insists on a higher cap (3x ARR or similar), we will need a commercial concession (discount or warranty bucket). Markus is the appropriate escalation for pricing tradeoffs.

5) Evidence & cooperation: Add a short evidence checklist (see attached template). Require customer to provide claim notice and relevant outputs; Redwood will not be bound to indemnify where customer fails to provide timely cooperation.

Priyom / Ben: confirm whether you want to offer the $1M floor + 12 months fees cap and whether commercial is prepared to move on pricing if customer insists on 3x. Ben, can we confirm SOC2 attestation availability and KMS options for Novaworks?

Kimberly
--
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Sally Nguyen <sally.nguyen@novaworks.com>, Novaworks Procurement <procurement@novaworks.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Output liability carveouts — Order Form redlines

Sally / team — thanks, and appreciate the quick turn. To keep momentum, here is a concrete proposal from Redwood (we can put this into the next redline):

- Indemnity trigger: Redwood will indemnify Novaworks for third-party IP infringement claims that assert unauthorized reproduction or use of third-party proprietary content in Redwoods model-generated outputs delivered to Novaworks end-users. The claim must identify the specific output(s).
- Exclusions: claims solely about the model training process are excluded unless Customer identifies reproductions in outputs. Open-source licensed content and Customer-provided content are carved out.
- Cap: greater of $1,000,000 or 12 months of committed Order Form fees (floor to protect smaller deals).
- Defense & settlement: Redwood to have initial defense control. Customer must consent to any settlement that admits liability or imposes injunctive/removal obligations; consent will not be unreasonably withheld. If parties cannot agree, escalate to senior legal/commercial teams with mediation option.
- Evidence/cooperation: customer must provide notice, copies of the allegedly infringing outputs, and relevant provenance. We will use the attached evidence-request-template.docx.

Next steps: Ill push an updated redline (NW_OrderForm_Redline_20270312.pdf) with exact language around definitions and the cap. If Novaworks signs off on the compromise above by COB Tuesday 2027-03-15, we can finalize without commercial concessions. If Novaworks insists on a 3x cap or broader trigger, please flag and we will escalate to Markus (commercial).

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Best,
Priyom
